🎓 Promote a Class

Move every student currently in one class to another in a single action — e.g. at the end of the year, moving all of "Grade 5" to "Grade 6" at once instead of editing each student individually.

🏫 Classes

Set up your school's classes once here, then add streams under each one (e.g. "Grade 5" → East / West). Once a class exists here, the Class and Stream fields on 🎓 Students turn into real dropdowns instead of free text — nothing breaks if you skip this, it's entirely optional.

Step 1: Generate your classes

Say how many grades/forms your school has and what to call them — this creates them all in one go. You can rename or remove any of them afterwards, and running this again only adds classes that don't already exist (it won't duplicate ones you've already renamed).

e.g. Prefix "Grade", count 6 → creates Grade 1 through Grade 6. Use "Form" instead for a secondary school.

Whole-School Register

Roll call for every registered student at once, regardless of class — useful for assemblies or a single school-wide daily register.

Your Classes

Tap a class to add its streams, take a register, or view its timetable.

📖 Subjects

This is your school-wide subject catalog — add every subject taught anywhere in the school once here (e.g. Mathematics, English, Physics, Biology, History, Geography). Then, from a class's own 🏫 Classes → Curriculum panel, mark which of these each class actually takes, either as core (everyone takes it) or as part of an elective choice (students pick one from a group, e.g. Physics vs Biology).

Class

Streams split this class into smaller groups — e.g. if "Grade 5" has two classes taught separately, add "East" and "West" here. Once added, they'll show up as a dropdown when registering a Grade 5 student, and each stream gets its own register and timetable below.

Roll call — mark who's present, for the whole class or just one stream.

Register History

Core subjects are taken by every student in this class. Elective subjects are grouped — e.g. a "Sciences" group containing Physics and Biology means each student picks one of the two, not both. Add subjects to the catalog on 📖 Subjects first if they're not in the list below yet.

Elective Groups

💳 Bill Payment Details

Shown on printed bills for customers who pay later — e.g. your Paybill/Till number and phone number. One line per detail.

📝 Receipt Notes

Extra lines printed at the bottom of every receipt and bill — e.g. "Terms and conditions apply" or "Goods once sold are not refundable." One line per statement.

🖼️ Shop Logo on Receipts

Printed at the very top of every receipt and bill. Any PNG/JPG works — it's shrunk to thermal-printer size automatically, so a large file is fine. Thermal printers are black-and-white: a bold, high-contrast logo prints far better than a pale or detailed one.

🔳 QR Code on Receipts

Printed at the bottom of every receipt and bill — e.g. your M-Pesa Paybill QR, your menu, your Google review link, or your socials. Upload the QR image itself (generate it wherever you like, then save the picture here). Keep it chunky: small, dense QR codes don't survive thermal printing.

📐 Receipt Position on the Paper

Use this when the roll isn't perfectly centred in your printer and receipts come out shifted. Preview it with any past sale from 📊 Daily Sales → Reprint.

Applies to the system print dialog and the on-screen receipt. Bluetooth/USB thermal printers are sent raw ESC/POS text, so this also sets their built-in left/centre/right justification.

📐 Receipt Size (System Print)

Sets the paper size the system print dialog uses automatically, so you don't have to set it there every time. Applies to the system print dialog only — Bluetooth/USB thermal printers use their own fixed roll width.

Most thermal printers cut automatically once the receipt is done — Auto is right for almost everyone. Only use Fixed length for pre-cut label stock or a printer that doesn't auto-cut.

Shrinks or enlarges everything on the receipt — useful if text is running slightly off the edge of your paper, or you want it more compact.

🖨️ Receipt Printer

Works with whichever printer mode is selected below. With "System print dialog", the dialog still opens once — this just removes the extra "Print" tap. For it to be fully silent too, launch Chrome with the --kiosk-printing flag (desktop only). With Bluetooth/USB, it prints straight away with no dialog at all.

Applies to every receipt and bill, on every printer. With "System print dialog" all copies go out as one job (one page per copy) — set the dialog's own copy count to 1 so you don't double up. With Bluetooth/USB they print back-to-back automatically.

Not connected.

Once connected, every receipt, bill, and printed report (Expenses, Restock, Sales Report) goes straight to this printer — no system print dialog.

Not connected.

Works with most generic USB thermal receipt printers, straight from the browser — no driver and no print dialog. If it doesn’t show up in the chooser, your printer likely needs a driver and won’t work over WebUSB; use "System print dialog" instead. Needs to be reconnected once per browser session. On Windows, if connecting fails with "Access denied," Windows already has a driver holding the printer exclusively — install Zadig, use it to replace that printer's driver with "WinUSB," then reconnect here.

With this on and this browser tab open, a phone with no printer of its own can send its receipts here instead of showing its own print dialog — useful if only this computer has a printer physically connected. Turns off automatically if the printer disconnects.

📷 Barcode Scanner

No pairing needed here — nearly all barcode scanners (USB or Bluetooth) act as a keyboard: they "type" the code and press Enter automatically. Just plug it in (or pair it as a Bluetooth keyboard in your device's Bluetooth settings), then scan.

  • On the 🛒 Sales Counter tab: scanning adds the item straight to the cart, from anywhere on the page.
  • On the 📦 Add New Items tab: scanning fills in the barcode, and looks up the product name automatically if it's a recognized product. If the item is already in your inventory, its existing details load so you can edit them.

Waiting for a scan...

🗄️ Cash Drawer

Cash drawers plug into the receipt printer itself (an RJ11/RJ12 port on the back), not into the computer directly — the printer sends it the "kick open" signal. Bluetooth and USB printer modes trigger this directly. "System print dialog" mode can now trigger it too, but only if your printer's driver is set to raw/"Generic / Text Only" mode (most thermal receipt printer drivers can be) — the kick command rides along inside the printed receipt itself. If your drawer doesn't open in that mode, switch the printer's driver to Generic / Text Only, or use Bluetooth/USB instead for guaranteed support.

🍳 Kitchen Order Tickets

When a sale includes one or more services, print a plain no-prices ticket for the kitchen — item names and quantities only, in large bold text. Uses the same printer as receipts (system dialog, or a connected Bluetooth/USB printer).

With "System print dialog", this opens a second print job right after the receipt's — expect two dialogs per sale. With Bluetooth/USB it just prints straight after the receipt with no extra tap.

🌐 Multi-Printer Network & Routing

Every till, phone, or tablet with this app open checks in here automatically, so you can see everything connected to this shop's POS in one place and decide which printer each kind of print job goes to — including sending one sale's receipt and kitchen ticket to two different printers at once.

The name and station shown to the rest of this shop for this device. To become a print destination other devices can route jobs to, also turn on "Let other devices at this shop print here too" above (needs a Bluetooth/USB printer connected).

Not loaded yet.

A destination is either a whole station (every online printer-holding device currently assigned to it) or one specific device. With no rules at all, a print job just goes to whichever single device is currently accepting jobs — same as before this feature existed.

📷 Camera Barcode Scanner

Uses this device's own camera as a barcode scanner — no separate scanner hardware needed. Once enabled, it runs silently in the background: nothing shown on screen, no camera preview, no button to press. Point the item's barcode at the camera anywhere a scan is accepted, and it behaves exactly like a normal handheld/USB scanner would. Works on Android (phone or a handheld POS terminal) and macOS; not supported on Windows/Linux desktop browsers.

Off.

🖥️ Customer / Pole Display

Shows only the running total on a small second screen facing the customer — no login, no other app screens reachable from it. Open it once on this device, drag its window onto the second screen, then press F11 there to go full-screen. It updates live as items are added, and briefly shows the amount tendered and change once a sale completes.

Works with any small monitor or tablet browser connected to (or mirroring) this device — it's just this same app opened to a second window, not special hardware.

📟 VFD Pole Display (hardware, e.g. Posiflex PD-2600 series, or generic/OEM units)

A real 2-line character display, connected by USB, rather than a second screen — writes the running total (and the amount tendered / change once a sale completes) straight to it, same moments the software display above updates. Connect it once, from this button — after that, it's detected and used automatically every time: on every app open, and even if it's unplugged and replugged while the app stays running. Chrome or Edge on desktop only.

Not connected.

These displays support several named modes (ADM, AEDEX, Epson, Futaba, Noritake, UTC), switched on the unit itself — usually a small DIP switch bank or an on-device menu. The two options above cover the two families those all fall into; tap Test after switching to see which one your unit actually needs. If neither shows correctly, check the unit's own switches/menu for its current mode.

Neither mode worked? Try raw bytes

If your display's manual or model number search turns up its exact command bytes (or a similar unit's), enter the initialize/clear command here as hex, space-separated (e.g. 1B 40 for Epson's ESC @, or 1B 52 40 for some ADM-family units) — text and a line break get sent the same way either mode does, so it's really just this one opening sequence that differs. Whatever works, tell me the bytes and I'll add it as a proper preset.

🗄️ Daily Backups

A snapshot of everything (inventory, sales, staff, settings — the whole shop) is taken automatically once a day, the first time any device syncs, before that day's changes are saved. Kept for 30 days. Use this if a bad sync or a mistake wipes out something important and you need to go back to an earlier day.

Tap "Refresh List" to check for available backups.

Restoring replaces EVERYTHING currently on every device with that day's snapshot — requires the management password, and the current state is itself saved as a safety copy first, just in case.

🗑️ Reset Inventory

Permanently removes every item AND service currently in Inventory, on every device. Sales history, customers, staff, and settings are not touched. A daily backup snapshot exists before this runs (see 🗄️ Backups above) in case it's a mistake.

♻️ Reset Sales & Stock History (Keep Items)

Permanently deletes every sale, bill, and stock movement record on every device — but the items themselves stay in Inventory. Any item with an opening stock recorded (see 📐 Stock Valuation on the Inventory tab) has its quantity put back to that opening figure; items with no opening stock recorded keep whatever quantity they currently have. Use "⚡ Declare All Undeclared as Opening Stock" first if you want every item to roll back cleanly. Customers, staff, expenses, and settings are not touched. This cannot be undone.

🚀 Purge Demo Data & Go Live

Been testing the app with fake sales and now ready to actually start using it? This is the same underlying reset as "Reset Sales, Keep Inventory" above, built specifically for that moment — with two extra options, a typed confirmation phrase on top of the management password, and a reminder to grab a copy of your test reports first if you want one. Your product catalog, prices, settings, staff accounts, and suppliers are never touched — only ⚠️ Reset Inventory above deletes items themselves, and that's a separate step if you want it.

🧾 Delete Voided Sales Records

A voided sale or bill is normally kept (struck-through) as an audit trail rather than deleted — see 🔒 Security & Access for how voiding itself works. This permanently ERASES every already-voided sale and bill instead of just hiding them, freeing up the list but also breaking that audit trail for good. Only sales/bills already marked voided are affected — nothing currently active is touched.

🔄 Reset App (Factory Reset)

Wipes this link back to a brand-new install — inventory, sales, customers, staff, passwords, and every setting are all cleared on every device sharing this link. Only the Business Name and Admin/Owner Name are kept, so the link itself still opens to the same shop identity, just empty. Separately-saved integrations (Payment Gateway, SMS, eTIMS, AI Capture List / Auto Product Images API keys) live outside this and are NOT cleared — turn those off individually in their own Settings sections first if you want those gone too. This cannot be undone — there is no backup restore that brings this back once it's run.

❓ Guide

Quick answers for the parts of this app that trip people up most. Tap a question to expand it.

💳 How do I get M-Pesa payments actually working?

You need one of two options, set up under ⚙️ Settings → 💳 Payment Gateway:

Option A — Paystack (simplest). Get a secret key (sk_live_... or sk_test_...) from your Paystack dashboard, paste it into "Save Paystack Key", and copy the Webhook URL shown underneath into Paystack Dashboard → Settings → API Keys & Webhooks. That's it — no Safaricom app needed.

Option B — Safaricom Daraja directly. Needs a Daraja app (Consumer Key/Secret), your Paybill or Till Number, and your Lipa Na M-Pesa Passkey. Use "Till Number" as the transaction type if you take payments on a Till, "Paybill" otherwise. The Callback URL is sent automatically with every request — you only need to copy it somewhere if Safaricom specifically asks you to pre-register one.

Once saved, the key/credential boxes disappear and are replaced with a green "✅ Payment configured" notice — that's confirmation it saved, not a sign something's hidden from you. There's no way to view a saved key again afterwards (this is deliberate, for security); to change it, use Reset to clear it and enter the new one.

If both Paystack and Daraja are configured at once, Paystack is used by default — force one specifically with the "Force a specific provider" dropdown at the bottom of that page.

🖨️ Which printer mode should I use, and why won't copies/the drawer work?

System print dialog works with any printer already installed on the device (via USB, network, or Windows/Mac driver) — no pairing needed, but it opens a print preview each time. Bluetooth and USB modes connect directly to a thermal receipt printer and print silently with no dialog at all, once paired/connected in this same Hardware settings page.

Multiple copies: set the number under "Number of Copies Printed per Receipt" — with System mode, all copies go out as ONE print job (one page per copy), so leave your printer driver's own copy count at 1 or you'll get double the copies you expect.

Cash drawer: it's the printer, not the computer, that triggers the drawer — it plugs into an RJ11/RJ12 port on the back of the printer. Bluetooth/USB modes trigger it directly. System dialog mode can too, but only if the printer's driver is set to "Generic / Text Only" (raw) mode — most thermal printer drivers support this in their settings.

Kitchen tickets use whichever printer mode is already selected here — there's currently no support for sending receipts and kitchen tickets to two different physical printers from the same device.

🖨️ How do I stop the print dialog from popping up every time?

No website or installed app — this one included — is allowed to print silently on its own. Browsers require a confirmation dialog every time; that's a security rule the browser enforces, not something any app's own code can switch off. Installing MinimartPOS to the home screen doesn't change this either.

Two real ways around it:

Bluetooth or USB thermal printer (Settings → Hardware) — these never open a dialog at all, since they send print data straight to the printer instead of going through the browser's print system. If you have a compatible thermal printer, this is the real fix.

Launch the browser with the --kiosk-printing flag — the standard trick for silent printing to a normal (non-thermal) printer via System dialog mode. Find the shortcut that installing MinimartPOS created, right-click → Properties, and add --kiosk-printing (with a space before it) to the end of the Target field. Close every open browser window first, then reopen from that shortcut. It'll auto-print to whichever printer is set as the Windows default, with no dialog and no way to pick a different one from the prompt — set the right default printer in Windows first.

📦🛠️ What's the difference between an Item and a Service?

Item — something sold exactly as it is: a bag of rice, a bar of soap. Has its own stock count and shows up in the Sales Counter.

Service — something you charge for without selling a physical unit: key cutting, delivery, installation. A plain service just has a flat price. Tick "Made from components" to link it to a bill of materials instead: add each item it uses and how much one sale uses (fractions like 1/2 work here), and the app then works out cost-per-sale and how many you can currently do from stock automatically. Tick "This is a bundle" instead to sell several items/services together (e.g. Paint + Brush + Roller) at one price — bundle components can be picked from existing stock (so their own stock is deducted correctly when it sells) or typed freely for something with nothing to track. A service is either component-based or a bundle, never both.
